organization.name: Example Co
organization.category: Customer onboarding software for B2B SaaS
organization.icp_summary: VP Customer Success / Head of Onboarding at 50–500 person B2B SaaS companies with a self-serve + sales-assisted motion.

off_pillar_policy: Log it. Dana will happily post about hiring all day — it draws founders, not buyers. Three weeks of the same off-pillar theme goes to REFRESH, not straight to the calendar.

pillars.name: Why customers quit in week one
pillars.definition: The first 30 days of a customer relationship: what actually causes a new account to disengage, how to see it coming in the data, and what a good week-one looks like. Practitioner-level specifics — cohort numbers, real failure modes, what Dana has watched break across 40 implementations.
in_scope: churn post-mortems and what the data showed
pillars.why_now: Baseline 2026-08-18: for 'why do new B2B SaaS customers churn in the first month', every source the answer used was a vendor blog post. No practitioner was cited. The topic is being answered badly by people with an incentive, which is the cheapest kind of pillar to take.

proof_assets.name: Cohort study across 40 implementations
proof_assets.notes: Dana has clearance to quote the 18% figure; check before quoting anything else from it

proof_assets.name: Ridgeline — cut week-one drop-off by half

incumbent.where: Company blogs, syndicated to LinkedIn company pages
incumbent.how_we_differ: Dana can publish real cohort numbers and name the failure modes; none of them will.

search_queries: onboarding handoff sales to CS failure

pillars.name: Saying the price out loud
pillars.definition: Dana's standing argument that hiding pricing costs more than it protects — what happened when Example Co published theirs, what buyers do when they can't find a number, and how to talk about price without discounting.
in_scope: what buyers do when pricing is hidden
pricing conversations in the sales cycle
pillars.why_now: This is the topic Dana argues about in comment threads unprompted, and the one buyers raise on first calls. It is also the one where she has a first-person result to report.

proof_assets.name: Published Example Co's pricing in 2025 — inbound and win-rate effect
proof_assets.notes: Dana has the before/after numbers; needs her OK to publish specifics

incumbent.who: A named pricing consultant with a large following
incumbent.strength: strong and consistent — expensive to displace outright
incumbent.how_we_differ: He advises; Dana did it and has the P&L consequence. First-person beats framework.

search_queries: B2B SaaS hidden pricing buyer behavior 2026

pillars.name: The people we build with
pillars.definition: Partners, integrations, and the practitioners Dana learns from — reposts with a real point of view attached, plus partner spotlights. Borrowed credibility and reciprocal reach, not filler.
in_scope: reposting named practitioners with Dana's own take
out_of_scope: reposting without a point of view
pillars.why_now: Employee and partner networks reach multiples of a company page's audience; this pillar is how Dana borrows reach she doesn't have yet.

proof_assets.name: Named repost list — REQUIRED, currently empty
proof_assets.notes: The agent cannot guess whose posts Dana respects. Until this list exists, every ask-list run should request it.

pillars.name: Building the team
pillars.definition: Hiring, culture, and founder life. Dana enjoys this and it performs, but it reaches founders rather than buyers. Kept as a secondary for rotation — no more than one post a month.
out_of_scope: anything that displaces a primary pillar slot
pillars.why_now: Performs on engagement, does not move pipeline. Capped on purpose.

notes: v1 from the 2026-08-18 BASELINE. Weights assume 3 posts/week: ~5 week-one-churn, ~4 pricing, ~3 partner proof per month. Partner-proof cannot produce ideas until Dana supplies the repost list — that ask is standing.
